pages.title: About Youyang Yu
pages.description: Youyang Yu is an artist, educator and community organiser, working across art, education and community.

hero.title: Hello, I’m Youyang.
hero.subtitle: Artist, filmmaker, educator & community organiser.
hero.intro: Born in China and educated in the UK, I work across animation, drawing, installation and participatory practice. I am interested in how inner experiences become visible, how we inhabit time, and how belonging grows between people.
hero.imageAlt: Youyang Yu, artist, filmmaker and educator.

blocks.title: Art, education and the spaces between us.
blocks.body:
I received my Master’s degree in Animation from the Royal College of Art in London. My films have screened internationally and have been collected by the British Film Institute and the Li Xianting Film Fund.

Alongside making films, I teach, curate and organise. I co-founded Feinaki Beijing Animation Week in 2019. More recently, my work has included community cultural coordination at CYC in Dali and the development of Wilder Mountain Dojo.

My practice carries experiences of living across China, the UK and the United States. Animation, objects, writing and shared encounters each offer a way to explore time, identity and belonging.

blocks.title: Current practice: Wilder Mountain Dojo
blocks.body: Wilder Mountain Dojo is a participatory public art project and a “life cultivation game” that invites people to see time as a flowing landscape, and to cultivate and play within. Through stories, body awareness, drawing and co-created cards, we make room for rest, expression and mutual support.

hero.intro: 出生于中国，在英国学习艺术。我通过动画、绘画、装置与参与式实践，探索内在经验如何变得可见，我们如何生活在时间中，以及归属如何在人与人之间生长。
hero.imageAlt: 俞悠洋，艺术家、教育者与社区组织者。

blocks.title: 艺术、教育，以及人与人之间的空间
blocks.body:
我毕业于英国皇家艺术学院动画专业，获硕士学位。作品入选多国电影节，并被英国电影协会和栗宪庭电影基金收藏。

创作影像的同时，我也从事教学、策展和组织工作。2019 年，我共同发起费那奇北京动画周。近期的实践包括大理 CYC 社区文化协调，以及「野山道场」的持续发展。

在中国、英国和美国生活的经历，进入了我的创作。动画、物件、文字和共同的相遇，分别提供了探索时间、身份与归属的方式。

pages.title: Begin with Pieces
pages.description: Animated short film adapted from Yuko Taniguchi's poem, made with AI in the loop for the Creativity Camp Study.

blocks.caption: Animated short film 'Begin with Pieces', 3 min, 2023

paras.html: Adapted from the poem of the same name by Yuko Taniguchi, the film flows through a synesthetic mental space — abstract painting and shimmering computer visuals held together by AI image generation, with a group of adolescents softly reciting the poem.

blocks.caption: Still from 'Begin with Pieces', 2023

paras.html: Yuko Taniguchi is also a collaborator on the Creativity Camp Study, an art–health–education research project run by educators, artists and scientists at the University of Minnesota. Its workshops use creativity and self-expression as tools for coping with depression, helping adolescents facing mental health challenges break out of negative thought patterns.
The film premiered in 2023 at the Weisman Art Museum, in 'The World Inside You' — an exhibition of work made by the young artists of the Creativity Camp.

pages.summary: A poem becomes a shared, shifting landscape of voices and images.

pages.title: Inheriting a Mountain
pages.description: A 2024 ceramic and video installation by Youyang Yu and Peng Wu, connecting a mountain on the frozen lake of Bdé Umáŋ with histories of migration and displacement.

blocks.caption: 'Inheriting a Mountain', 2024, ceramic and video installation by Youyang Yu and Peng Wu; photographed on the ice of Bdé Umáŋ / Lake Harriet, Minneapolis

paras.html: A mountain, carried into a landscape of lakes.

The work responds to the jade mountain in the collection of the Minneapolis Institute of Art. Its presence in Minnesota becomes a point of departure for thinking about migration, displacement, and the ways personal narratives meet larger histories.

Peng Wu and I made a mountain out of clay, carried it onto the frozen lake of Bdé Umáŋ, also known as Lake Harriet, and sat down with it across a table. The ceramic and video installation brings that encounter into conversation with the histories carried by objects and people.

pages.summary: A ceramic mountain, a frozen lake, and questions of displacement and belonging.

pages.title: Inside My Eyes

blocks.caption: Animated short film 'Inside My Eyes', 2 min 35s, 2D digital

paras.html: Sometimes, thoughts might get heavy. Yuko found a trick to offload her overwhelming thoughts to some magical elephants inside her mind.
Imagined in collaboration with AI, frame-by-frame digital watercolor histology of a contemplating racing brain.

An animated short film directed by Youyang Yu, based on Yuko Taniguchi's poem 'Inside My Eyes', inspired by her long term efforts in collaboration with psychiatrist Dr. Kathryn Cullen exploring the impact of creative practices on the wellbeing of adolescents facing pressing mental health challenges.
I incorporated AI image processing in the making of the film.
Primarily I used stable diffusion for quick visual concepts of the background designs, runway inpainting model for greenscreen, to separate the elephants and butterflies from found footage.

During production, I used ebsynth for quick rotoscoping of the elephant's silhouette, and after digitally sketch drawn some frame-by-frame animation, then img2img in stable diffusion to batch render the final painted / ink/ watercolor/ biogenic histology look which is traditionally very time-consuming and expensive to create even just for one image, let alone to keep shapes in consistency from sequential frames due to these analog medium's freeform physical nature.

blocks.caption: An AI-processed biogenic histology example in the film

paras.html: Inside my eyes
Sometimes, my thoughts fly around
inside my mind like a sand storm.
So I sit and shut my eyes, which is when
those enormous elephants mysteriously appear-
They come as a tribe, slowly walk across my mind.
I watch each elephant, each with a different color
of skin, coarse and wrinkly. These colorful elephants are
here for a moment like a rainbow after hard rain.
Their large feet are pressing until
my ground is solid and strong.
When I open my eyes, they are gone.
They always come to me in the midst of my sand storm.
Elephants have incredible memories.
They never forget where they have been.
Next time, I will walk
with my elephants.
Yuko Taniguchi

pages.title: For the Best

blocks.caption: Animated Short Film 'For the Best' 2015, 3min25s, Collected by the British Film Institute

paras.html: However laborious it is, hand drawn animation communicates emotion at a level no other medium can achieve. In this project, I especially wanted to affirm my most treasured personal memory, an unrequited love between two men, through drawing with my own hand frame by frame.

To save it from vanishing afar, it’s something I had to do. If I didn't grab it on time, the flesh of the experience would soon be gone forever, eventually the intense feeling will become a faded mark, like most people trying hard to remember what it was like being so passionate about that specific person, but paralyzed to do so because it has never really happened. I thought what I had at that moment was something precious, needed to be shared and validated, and that outcome was this short animation, 'For the Best'.

pages.summary: A hand-drawn memory of unrequited love between two men.

cardZh.title: 最好结局
cardZh.description: 以逐帧手绘，留住两名男性之间一段未被回应的爱。

paras.html: Our existence is just a surge of fluctuation pulsing through the timeline. The perspective of being alive only exists in the present. Though innate to our life, the past and the future is always absent, which easily narrows our understanding of the world to a thin slice.

In my graduation project I love you forever now, I want to portray our shared mortality by looking into the idea of our past and future self, to examine our understanding of the concept 'myself', question its stability and spot our unawareness towards not just ourselves, but also other people's connected and fluid identity, who all experience the same mortal life as vivid and as complex as 'me'.

pages.title: Feinaki Beijing Animation Week

paras.html: Feinaki Beijing Animation Week is an independent animation festival I co-founded in 2019 and ran as operational director through its 2019 and 2020 editions. Built from nothing into an international community of independent animators, it pairs an annual week of screenings in Beijing with curated programmes through the year, online and off. Cartoon Brew and CGTN described it as the event bringing world independent animation to Chinese audiences.

Selected programmes: the 2020 Feinaki global special screening with abC Art Book Fair and Times Museum; the RCA 30-year animation retrospective, 2019; and an online series with animation directors from around the world. For the 2020 edition I also curated an artist talk and wrote Fringes of (Chinese) Animation for the International Short Film Festival Winterthur.

pages.title: Wilder Mountain Dojo / 野山道场
pages.description: A participatory public art project and “life cultivation game” for rest, expression and mutual support. Basecamp workshops are planned for the Twin Cities in November 2026.

hero.eyebrow: Wilder Mountain Dojo · 野山道场
hero.title: A space to rest. Permission to grow.
hero.subtitle: Basecamp: To Play with Time that Is… Murdering Us
hero.intro: Is it the ticking clock that is chasing us, or the meaning of time we adopted from society that is measuring and managing us?

blocks.title: A space to receive support, and catch your breath.
blocks.body:
Wilder Mountain Dojo is a participatory public art project and a “life cultivation game” that invites people to see time as a flowing landscape, and to cultivate and play within. It is created and led by Youyang Yu, an artist, educator and community organiser who lives a transnational life between China, the UK and the US.

To my fellow diasporic friends, doing our best to support ourselves while navigating change, restlessness and uncertainty.

I want to create a protected time and space with you: somewhere to slow down, sense the body, express feelings that have not yet found their form, connect with inner strength, and practise receiving and giving support. Like a newly sprouted seed, or a child learning to walk, we can be allowed to explore, be uncertain and grow, rather than be measured as finished products.

blocks.title: Basecamp: To Play with Time that Is… Murdering Us
blocks.body:
Twin Cities, Minnesota · November 2026
Three two-hour adult workshops are planned at three venues, on three Saturday afternoons. Basecamp is supported by the Watson Foundation Enlight Fellowship. Dates: Saturdays 7, 14 and 21 November, 1–3 pm. Venue details will be announced.

This round, I invite you to reimagine your relationship with time, and find alignment with the rhythms of your own life.

blocks.title: When even rest becomes a task.
blocks.body: When instability, the pressure to improve and a heavy workload arrive together, finding time to rest becomes difficult in itself. Even when exhaustion forces us to stop, we may still feel that we should work harder, become more efficient and optimise ourselves into someone good enough. Rest can become the next task to complete.

blocks.title: An alliance across time.
blocks.body:
We will begin by coming back to the body: meditating and moving together, feeling how the body is right now, noticing the patterns of action we keep repeating, and drawing what the body feels. We will also try imagining the self as a collective continually changing through time, allowing who you are now to form an alliance with yourself at different stages of life: understanding the self who worked so hard in the past, caring for present needs, and leaving some room for the future self.

A rhythm of rest and work can become a promise kept between allies. Practice begins with a small, real action: acknowledging the body’s limits, protecting a little time to rest, or expressing a need. Through listening and responding together, we practise bringing those needs into relationships, exploring how to receive support, offer support and build reciprocity.

blocks.title: The afternoon, in four parts.
blocks.body:
Back to the body. I open with a short talk on coming back to the body and noticing the patterns of action we keep repeating. Then we meditate, walk, stop, and feel how the body is right now.

Draw what you feel. Paper and paint are on the floor. No sketching, nothing has to look good, and nothing has to be shown.

Co-create cards. Everyone makes two cards: a pattern of action you keep repeating and don't like, and one you like, a repeated action that supports you and the people around you across time.

Share. In circles of three or four, we share our cards and what we noticed. Speak if you want to, listen if you'd rather. I close by thanking everyone who joined this co-creation.

blocks.title: Make two cards. Leave a little support.
blocks.body:
At each workshop, I will invite you to make two practice cards of your own: one for a pattern of action you keep repeating and don’t like, and one for a repeated action you like, one that supports you and the people around you across time. We close by sharing our cards and what we noticed. You will take a creation home and can leave a card in Wilder Mountain Dojo’s growing shared deck—a contribution for the next person practising self-support through partings, reunions and upheaval.

We hope to begin with a real room and an encounter we care for together: somewhere rest can happen, and inner and collective strength can gradually grow.

blocks.title: A practice taking shape.
blocks.body: One ink self-reflection painting workshop has taken place during Watson’s in-person immersive. Talks and exchanges at the CYC community in Dali are another part of the wider practice. Basecamp is the next invitation to gather.

blocks.title: A name drawn from moving landscapes.
blocks.body:
In a 2023 invitation to share nomadic narratives, “wild mountains” named the layered landscapes encountered through a life of movement. A dojo was imagined as a place of practice: a rehearsal room for expression, a group for autobiographical creation, and a shared narrative space. Belonging could grow through participation.

First, let a room become real. Then the mountain has room to grow.

hero.eyebrow: 野山道场 · Wilder Mountain Dojo
hero.title: 和追杀我们的​时间，切磋切磋
hero.subtitle: Basecamp · 让休息有地方发生
hero.intro: 追杀我们的，是滴答作响的时钟，还是我们从社会中接受的、正在衡量和管理我们的那套时间意义？

blocks.title: 能得到支持、也能喘息的空间
blocks.body:
野山道场是一个参与式公共艺术项目，也是一场「人生修行游戏」，邀请大家把时间认作流动的大地，修行其间，在玩耍里成长。它由在中国、英国和美国之间跨国生活的艺术家、教育者和社区组织者俞悠洋发起并带领。

给在变化、不停歇与不确定中，努力撑住自己的离乡同路人。

我想和你们一起创造一段被护佑的时间与空间：在这里，可以慢下来，感知身体，表达尚未成形的心声，连接内在的力量，也练习接受和给予支持。像刚发芽的种子、像孩子学习迈步那样被允许探索、不确定和生长，而不是被当成完成品来衡量。

blocks.title: Basecamp：和追杀我们的时间，切磋切磋
blocks.body:
明尼苏达双子城 · 2026 年 11 月
计划在三个场地、三个周六下午，分别举办一场两小时的成人工作坊，由 Watson Foundation Enlight Fellowship 支持发起。日期：11 月 7、14、21 日，三个周六下午 1–3 点；场地信息将另行公布。

这一轮，我邀请你和我一起，重新想象自己与时间的关系，与自己的生命节律重新对齐。

blocks.title: 当休息，也成了一项任务
blocks.body: 当生活里同时压着动荡、提升的压力和工作量的忙碌，「找到休息的时间」本身就成了一件难事。我们也许已经在筋疲力尽后被迫停下，却仍然觉得自己应该更努力、更有效率、更快优化调整成为一个足够好的人。连休息，都可能变成下一项需要完成的任务。

blocks.title: 与时间中的自己结盟
blocks.body:
在工作坊里，我们会从回到身体开始：一起冥想、活动，感受身体此刻的样子，留意自己一再重复的行动模式，再把身体里的感受画出来。我们也会尝试把「自己」想象成一个在时间中持续变化的集体，让此刻的你与人生不同阶段的自己结盟：理解过去那个努力生活的自己，照顾此刻的需要，为未来的自己留下一些余地。

有节律的休息与工作，可以成为同盟之间的一次守约。练习从一个小而真实的行动开始：承认身体的限度，为自己保留一段休息，或说出一个需要。在共同倾听与回应中，我们也练习把这些需要带入关系，探索如何接受支持、给予支持，与彼此建立互惠。

blocks.title: 那天下午，分四段
blocks.body:
回到身体。我先讲一小段：回到身体，留意自己一再重复的行动模式。然后一起冥想，走动、停下，感受身体此刻的样子。

画出感受。纸和颜料都在地上。不打草稿，不求好看，画完也可以不给任何人看。

共创卡牌。每人做两张卡：一张是你不喜欢、却一再重复的行动模式；一张是你喜欢的、跨越时间支持自己和身边人的重复行动。

分享交流。三四人一圈，交流各自的卡和觉察。想说的人说，只想听的人听。最后，我会谢谢每一位加入这场共创的人。

blocks.title: 带走一张创作，留下一份助力
blocks.body:
每一场工作坊，我都会邀请你创作两张属于自己的「修行」卡牌：一张写下你不喜欢、却一再重复的行动模式，一张写下你喜欢的、跨越时间支持自己和身边人的重复行动。最后，我们围坐分享各自的卡与觉察。你将带走一份创作，也可以在野山道场共同生长的牌堆里留下一张卡，为下一个在聚散与动荡中练习自我支持的人，留下一份助力。

我们希望从一间真实的屋子、一次共同守护的相遇开始，让休息有地方发生，让内在与集体的力量慢慢长出来。

blocks.title: 实践正在发生
blocks.body: 野山道场已在 Watson 线下 immersive 举办过一场水墨自我照见绘画工作坊。在大理 CYC 社区的分享与交流，也构成了这项实践的一部分。Basecamp 是下一次共同聚集的邀请。

blocks.title: 名字来自流动的风景
blocks.body:
2023 年的《游牧叙事征集信》以「在无根处，被看见并感到归属」为题。「野山」是离散生活中不断看见的风景的叠加；「道场」是求道之所，也可以是表达排练室、自传创作小组和一个共同的叙事空间。归属感由共同参与逐渐形成。

先让一间屋子真实出现，整座山才有资格慢慢长出来。

pages.title: Writing
pages.description: Writing by Youyang Yu on identity, time, the body and independent animation.

hero.title: Thinking in fragments, finding a thread.
hero.intro: Writing is part of the practice: a place to stay with questions about identity, time, the body and the worlds we make together.

blocks.title: A life still unfinished.
blocks.body:
Work in progress · Excerpt translated from the Chinese draft

“I have been writing this letter for more than two years.

It began with the existential question ‘Who am I?’ and gradually found its way into the illusion of time, systemic oppression, and the hidden structures of embodied practice.

I discovered that I was only the tip of the iceberg of the conditions of my time.

… In this age of collective sleeplessness, I struggled to write a narrative of dawn—then realised that dawn arrives of its own accord.”

The Chinese working title is 你命运半写就，人生未完成，站在因果冰山上寻求自由. This excerpt is from an ongoing, five-part writing project.

blocks.title: 你命运半写就，人生未完成，站在因果冰山上寻求自由。
blocks.body:
写作中 · 节选

这一封信，我写了2年多。

从拆解「我是谁」这一存在主义大问开始，逐步写入时间幻象、系统压迫与具身修行的隐秘结构。

我发现自己只是我所身处的时代症候的冰山一角。

这个既是天地间自然共存，又由社会中无数「他人面孔」交织而成的关系网络，仅用「系统」来命名，似乎并不足够精确。

我又尝试用剧本分析、日常观察、可视化案例补充概念的空洞。

冬去春来夏忙碌，又入冬逢新春夏。

生成的小径时隐时现，我走得缓慢又惊险，在这个集体失眠的时代，我苦苦写一篇黎明的叙事，然后惊觉黎明无需叙写，它自行到来。

这是一组持续写作、分为五个大章的文字。此处收录开篇节选。

pages.title: Earlier studio notes

paras.html: These earlier studio notes preserve animation process, teaching and festival material from the previous website. For my current practice and contact details, visit About.

Born in China and trained in the UK, Youyang received his Master's degree in animation from the Royal College of Art in London and has exhibited his work internationally across Europe, Asia, and North & South America.
In 2019 he co-founded Feinaki Beijing Animation Week, an independent animation festival. He teaches, curates and organises between China and the United States.

A snippet of my hand-drawn animation 'For the Best' (2015), collected by the British Film Institute

paras.html: As a traditionally trained 2D animation artist researching the field of generative AI and multi-sensory digital transformation, I am constantly in awe of the nonstop technological breakthroughs I witness, yet often look back to my pen and brushes that inspired me to make art and build my deep emotional connections with the physical touch in the first place.

blocks.caption: Still Frame from 'For the Best'(2015), AI transformation experiment 2022
Clip from AI-augmented animation short 'Inside My Eyes' 2023

paras.html: I try to create art that combines both innovative digital tools and the traditional tactile artistic mediums that speak to the multitude of daring innovations and deeply bonded emotional engagement in the continuum of creative expressions.

blocks.caption: Clip from AI-augmented animation short 'Inside My Eyes' 2023

paras.html: My recent animation film 'Inside My Eyes'(2023) based on Japanese writer Yuko Taniguchi's poem, explores an overwhelmed mind space organically painted in motion in the watercolor/ oil/ biogenic histology look only enabled by the power of AI image generation.
Still frames from 'Inside My Eyes' 2023, img2img AI-augmentation experiment

blocks.caption: Still from 'Begin with Pieces', 2023

paras.html: A second film followed the same year. Begin with Pieces (2023) takes another Yuko Taniguchi poem into a synesthetic mind-space, recited by the adolescents of the Creativity Camp Study and premiered at the Weisman Art Museum.

blocks.caption: 'Inheriting Mountain on Land of 10,000 Lakes', 2024, ceramic installation on the ice of Bdé Umáŋ, Minneapolis
Working in a film crew as onset assistant director in Sino-U.S international coproduction 'Crazy Alien', 2017
Working in a film crew as onset assistant director in Sino-U.S international coproduction 'Crazy Alien', 2017

paras.html: As someone who has lived a nomadic life often traveling between distinctly different cultures, I feel like an alien body to most of the places where I live and worked, yet I believe my bilingual background and multicultural perspective equipped me to become a skilled people person who holds critical world views but can communicate with an open mind in great patience, which manifested from my diverse working experience in leading art workshops, organizing film festivals, public speaking, directing and assisting film productions.

blocks.caption: Leading and co-instructing various art workshops in Beijing, 2018-2021

paras.html: In 2020, as the operational director of Feinaki Animation Week, I was invited to curate an artist talk alongside writing an article about Chinese independent animation for the International Short Film Festival Winterthur in Switzerland, which was then published on the film critic website 'Talking Shorts'.

blocks.caption: Being a co-founder and the operational director at Feinaki Beijing Animation Week, 2019-2020

paras.html: Thank you for your patience in spending time to know me, you're most likely already my friend:)
I am grateful for all the opportunities to connect, collaborate, learn from, and grow with the community of like-minded artists, educators, and innovators.

pages.title: CYC Community, Dali
pages.description: Youyang Yu hosts CYC, 706’s residency community in Dali, and is designing a community operating system from it.

blocks.caption: CYC members with their drawings, Dali, 2026

paras.html: Since January 2026 I have hosted CYC, 706’s residency community in Dali, Yunnan. With a weekly rhythm of gatherings, talks and shared meals, the local group grew from 180 to a full 500 members, and a second group is now growing.

Having lived a nomadic life between countries, I am designing a “community operating system” from this house: practices and tools that let members reconnect easily after time apart, and turn a place people pass through into a network of support. Talks and exchanges for Wilder Mountain Dojo also happen here.
